source: a16z Podcast — Is AI a bubble? Data centers, GPUs, and the AI economy
summary: Cursor has accumulated enough coding tokens that it will become increasingly difficult for incumbent public coding companies to catch up.
summary_extended: Baker argues that Cursor has accumulated approximately one trillion coding tokens, which he believes is approaching or has reached the threshold at which a durable data moat becomes established, making it increasingly difficult for incumbent public coding companies to close the gap. His reasoning is that token accumulation compounds over time — the more coding interactions Cursor processes, the better its models become, creating a self-reinforcing advantage that rivals cannot easily replicate without a comparable data flywheel. Baker expresses surprise that no publicly traded coding software company has attempted to compete by subsidizing an AI coding product at break-even using cash flows from their existing profitable legacy business, suggesting this strategic window is closing. The investment implication is bearish on incumbent public coding software companies that have not yet mounted a credible AI coding response, though Baker frames this as an observation and concern rather than a high-conviction trade. No specific public companies are named, and Cursor itself is private, limiting direct investable expression of this thesis.
detail: Cursor now has a trillion tokens of coding data. There is a point at which the token accumulation creates a durable data moat. Baker expresses surprise that no public coding company has tried to compete by running at break-even using their existing profitable business as a subsidy. The window to catch up is closing.
confidence_evidence: Baker frames this as a concern/observation rather than a definitive prediction, using 'I think' and 'there will be a point.'
quote_fragment: cursor now has a trillion tokens and it will be tough to catch them
